  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Anyone who gets hold of a share link can read the document, forever",
      "scenario": "A share link is pasted into a chat, an email thread, a ticket or a browser history, or it is forwarded by a recipient. Because no login is required and the link has no expiry, any attacker who later obtains the URL (insider, support agent, someone browsing an archived thread, a compromised mailbox) reads the document in full. There is no way to cut off access once the link is out.",
      "component": "Public file viewer",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in. Links never expire." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613", "CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "A shared link works for anyone who finds it and never stops working, so one leaked link means permanent access.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Share links must expire and be revocable",
        "given": "a user has created a public share link for a document",
        "when": "the link's expiry time passes, or the owner revokes the link",
        "then": "the viewer endpoint rejects the request with 404/410 and no file content or metadata is returned"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Guessable or enumerable link tokens let attackers find other people's files",
      "scenario": "If the share URL contains a sequential id, a database id, a filename or a short token, an attacker scripts requests across the token space and harvests documents belonging to other users. Nothing else gates access because the design requires no login, so each correct guess is an immediate full read of someone else's file.",
      "component": "Share link generator",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Users upload documents and share them through a public link. Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639", "CWE-330"],
      "plainLanguage": "If link addresses are predictable, someone can try lots of them and download strangers' documents.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Share tokens must be unguessable",
        "given": "a share link is generated for an uploaded document",
        "when": "the token is created",
        "then": "it uses at least 128 bits from a cryptographically secure random source, is not derived from the file id, name or user id, and enumeration attempts are rate limited and alerted"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Public S3 bucket or direct object URLs bypass the application entirely",
      "scenario": "Files live in S3. If the bucket or objects are made world readable, or the app hands out raw object URLs, attackers reach files without ever touching the share-link check. A world readable bucket also allows ListObjects, letting an attacker download every document any user has ever uploaded in a single pass.",
      "component": "S3 storage integration",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Files are stored in an S3 bucket." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-732", "CWE-425"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the cloud storage bucket itself is public, people can grab all the files without using the share link at all.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Files are only reachable through the application",
        "given": "documents stored in the S3 bucket",
        "when": "a viewer requests a file via a valid share link",
        "then": "the bucket blocks all public access and listing, and the app streams the file or issues a short lived pre-signed URL scoped to that single object"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Uploaded HTML or SVG runs as script on the sharing domain",
      "scenario": "An attacker uploads an .html or .svg 'document' and shares the link. When a victim opens it, the browser executes attacker script in the origin that serves shared files.       "component": "Public file viewer",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Users upload documents and share them through a public link." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79", "CWE-434"],

        "title": "Shared files are served inertly",

        "when": "the response is sent to the browser",
        "then": "it uses Content-Disposition: attachment, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, a server-determined safe content type, and is served from a separate sandbox domain"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "The service becomes a malware and phishing distribution host",
      "scenario": "Because upload and viewing need no account, an attacker uploads malware or a credential phishing page and distributes the resulting link, which never expires. Victims trust the organisation's domain. The result is harm to third parties, domain and IP reputation damage, and blocklisting of the service by browsers and mail filters.",
      "component": "File upload endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in. Links never expire." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-434"],
      "plainLanguage": "Attackers could use your file sharing to host viruses or fake login pages on your own web address.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Uploads are scanned and takedown is possible",
        "given": "a file is uploaded for sharing",
        "when": "the upload completes and before the link becomes usable",
        "then": "the file is scanned by malware detection, an allow list of file types is enforced, and an operator can disable any link immediately"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Unauthenticated uploads and unlimited downloads drive storage and bandwidth cost",
      "scenario": "With no login on the flow, an attacker scripts large or numerous uploads to fill the S3 bucket, and hammers a single large public link to generate egress charges. Since links never expire, storage is never reclaimed. The result is a cost-based denial of service and degraded availability for real users.",
      "component": "File upload endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Users upload documents and share them through a public link." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770", "CWE-400"],
      "plainLanguage": "Without limits, someone can upload endless huge files or download one link millions of times and run up your cloud bill.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Quotas on upload and download",
        "given": "an upload request or a share link download",
        "when": "a per-file size, per-account storage quota, per-IP upload rate or per-link download/bandwidth cap is exceeded",
        "then": "the request is rejected with 413 or 429 and the owner and operators are alerted"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Share links leak to search engines and third parties through referrers",
      "scenario": "Because the link alone grants access, any place it travels is a disclosure channel. Crawlers index pages that embed the link, making private documents searchable.       "component": "Public file viewer",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Users upload documents and share them through a public link. Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V3.4.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "Secret links can end up in Google results or be sent to other websites in the browser's referrer header.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Prevent link leakage",
        "given": "a share link is opened in a browser",
        "when": "the viewer page renders or the user navigates away",
        "then": "the response sets Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, and robots.txt disallows the share path"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No record of who viewed or uploaded a document",
      "scenario": "Viewers are anonymous by design and uploads are not tied to an authenticated identity, so after a leak the team cannot tell whether a document was accessed, by whom, or how often. An insider who forwards a link, or an attacker who enumerated tokens, leaves nothing attributable, and breach notification obligations cannot be assessed.",
      "component": "Public file viewer",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Since viewers never log in, you cannot tell who read a leaked document or prove whether anything was taken.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Access events are recorded per share link",
        "given": "a share link is accessed",
        "when": "the file is served",
        "then": "the link id, timestamp, source IP, user agent and bytes served are logged, and the owner can see an access history for their link"
      }
    }
  ]
}
